faq.q: Why is the Burj Khalifa shaped like that?
faq.a: Its Y-shaped plan and spiralling setbacks make it stiff and break up the wind's whirlpools, so the 828-metre tower sways much less than a plain shape would.
asks: Why does the Burj Khalifa get thinner at the top?

faq.a: When wind flows past a tall, blunt object, swirls of air called vortices peel off alternately from each side. Each one gives the object a sideways tug, so it can be pushed back and forth.
asks: Why do tall buildings sway sideways in wind?

faq.q: Why are wind whirlpools a problem for skyscrapers?
faq.a: The alternating tugs come in a regular rhythm. If it matches the building's natural sway, the swaying can grow large and uncomfortable, so engineers design to avoid it.
asks: How does wind make buildings vibrate?

faq.q: How do setbacks confuse the wind?
faq.a: Setbacks change the building's width at different heights. Because the rhythm of the vortices depends on the width, each level sheds them at a different rhythm, so they never add up into one big push.
asks: What are setbacks on a skyscraper?

faq.q: What is the Burj Khalifa's buttressed core?
faq.a: It is a central hexagonal concrete core braced by three wings, forming a Y shape. Each wing supports the others, making the tower extremely stiff against wind and twisting.
asks: How is the Burj Khalifa built?

facts: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai, completed in 2010, is 828 metres tall, the tallest building in the world.
The Burj Khalifa's shape was refined through many wind tunnel tests to reduce vortex shedding.
